title: Land Flipping — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: Buy Below Value, Market With Discipline, and Verify Every Acre: Worksheets for the land flipping business model, direct mail and texting engines, compliant outbound, raw-land list building, sold-comp pricing, and perc, septic, and site due diligence

worksheets.title: Business Model and Direct Mail Engine
worksheets.purpose: Lock in the buy price, county selection, parcel scrub, offer math, and direct mail economics that turn scrubbed county lists into signed contracts with vacant landowners who own free and clear.
instructions: Work through one target county at a time and complete every field before pulling a list or paying for a single mail piece or text.
Use sold land-only numbers for every price input, and write each figure as a specific dollar amount, percentage, or count rather than a range you hope for.
Cite the practitioner benchmark you are measuring against next to each answer so later campaign results can be compared to a known standard.
Revisit fields five through ten after every completed mail drop and update the ratios with your own conversations had and cash collected.
Do not move to the outbound and data worksheet until funding for six months of drops is set aside and the completion gate below is signed.

fields.name: target_buy_percentage
fields.prompt: Write the exact percentage of market value you will pay for vacant parcels, and explain where that number sits against the practitioner range of 5% to 30%, 50% to 55%, and roughly 80% with subdividing to manufacture margin.
fields.example: Target buy: 30% to 40% of market value through direct mail, the band the Apke Brothers describe [Apke Brothers — U4C3AVYK9M4 @ 00:00:01]. Deep-discount floor reference: Seth Williams buys at 5% to 30% of value, and one REtipster parcel bought for $4,587 sold for $20,000 [REtipster — pBstDNy9IuM @ 00:10:47]. Anything above 55% requires a subdivide plan before signing.

fields.name: county_selection_criteria
fields.prompt: List the counties you will market to and prove each one clears the volume screen: annual land sales count, active listings versus sold listings, and days on market. Note which small counties must be bundled with neighbors before a campaign launches.
fields.example: Ocala-area target county: 412 land sales last year, fewer active listings than sold listings, and median days on market of 74, so it clears the 200-sale floor Thomas uses [Thomas | Land Flipping — ZfyoS572Kbk @ 00:52:56]. A smaller neighbor produced only 780 text records, so it gets bundled with adjoining counties to avoid burnout [Thomas | Land Flipping — ZfyoS572Kbk @ 02:01:35].

fields.name: parcel_scrub_rules
fields.prompt: Define the scrub rules you will run on every pulled list before an offer is priced. Name each disqualifier, such as wetlands, flood zone, steep slope, or missing access, and estimate what share of the raw list you expect to remove.
fields.example: Remove parcels with wetlands, flood zone, slope, or bad access, which strips 40% to 50% of a county list. Then delete the 30% to 40% of DataTree records that are garbage before any letter is merged [Sumner Healey — R4icAmTE4WI @ 00:04:05]. Map-only frontage gets flagged: sometimes it looks like you have access, but you don't [DealMachine Podcast — HE45qWS8txg @ 00:12:30].

fields.name: offer_formula
fields.prompt: Show the math behind your offer price for one county. Start from the median price per acre of sold comps, subtract agent, closing, and lender costs, then apply your target buy percentage and write the final per-acre offer number.
fields.example: Median sold price is $10,000 per acre; subtract agent, closing, and lender costs to reach a net resale figure, then apply the target percentage to land the per-acre offer. Every county is priced from a few great comps and acreage bands before upload, never auto-priced, since one user sent 50,000 mailers and got 2 deals [Apke Brothers — JRIbKp3FaEs @ 00:04:01].

fields.name: channel_mix_roas
fields.prompt: Decide your opening channel mix between direct mail and texting, and record the return on ad spend you will hold each channel to. Explain how you will split budget if one channel outperforms the other over the first ninety days.
fields.example: Texting carries the larger share because Landon Bleau reports about 9x return on ad spend for texts versus about 3x for mail, with texting producing 60% to 70% of deals [REtipster — Uaqe67xWZN0 @ 00:38:55]. Mail stays in the mix at a 5x floor, matching the low end of the 5 to 10x band Clayton Hepler reports [DealMachine Podcast — HE45qWS8txg @ 00:09:38].

fields.name: marketing_volume_per_deal
fields.prompt: Estimate how many mailers or texts you must send to close one deal, and multiply that by your per-piece cost. Write the resulting marketing spend per deal next to the average profit you expect, and flag the gap.
fields.example: Model one deal per 2,500 mailers at about 60 cents each, or roughly $1,500 of marketing per deal against about $18,500 net [Apke Brothers — U4C3AVYK9M4 @ 00:01:03]. Stress case: 6,000 to 8,000 mailers or 30,000 to 40,000 texts per deal at about $25K average profit, still a clearly positive return on every closed deal [DealMachine Podcast — HE45qWS8txg @ 00:09:38].

fields.name: mail_cost_and_runway
fields.prompt: Record your all-in cost per mail piece and the monthly volume you can sustain. Confirm in writing that your cash covers at least six months of drops, including slow early results, before the first batch leaves the print house.
fields.example: All-in cost is $0.69 per piece with no minimum, the same price for 1 or 10,000 pieces [Apke Brothers — cFfiZJm0txo @ 00:30:07]. At 2,000 pieces a month that is $1,380 monthly, so six months of runway equals $8,280 set aside before the first drop [Apke Brothers — cFfiZJm0txo @ 00:08:16]. Funding stays separate from purchase capital for parcels.

fields.name: offer_letter_style
fields.prompt: Choose your letter format, whether blind priced offer, neutral letter, or range letter, and justify it. Describe what goes inside the envelope, including any enclosed purchase agreement, and how you will confirm merged pricing before the full drop.
fields.example: Blind priced offer, because the seller needs a number to react to. A one-page purchase agreement rides in the envelope, and sellers have texted back a photo of the signed agreement [Land Investing Pros — gMTr4Kngzx8 @ 00:05:52]. A merged proof of 10 to 20 letters confirms the offer price variable before the full drop [Land Insights — Tj5JsRK_YdQ @ 00:29:27].

fields.name: template_tracking
fields.prompt: Assign a reference number to every mailer or text template you run. Describe the tracking sheet you will keep, including conversations had and cash collected per template, and state the rule for when you double down on a winner.
fields.example: Template M-01 is the long handwritten letter and M-02 is the short priced postcard, each stamped with its reference number and logged for conversations had and cash collected [Olufemi Ajose — tF_EbilAGj4 @ 00:14:48]. Text openers get trimmed to roughly 100 characters, the change that lifted Landon Bleau's reply rate from 13% toward nearly 20% [REtipster — Uaqe67xWZN0 @ 00:43:33].

fields.name: remail_and_stale_leads
fields.prompt: Write your remail calendar and stale-lead rules. State how many months you wait before remailing a list that produced zero deals, how you handle sellers who said no, and how long old leads stay in active follow-up.
fields.example: Lists that flop get remailed after 3 months, since one mailer got zero deals and the same data remailed three months later made $100,000 [Sumner Healey — R4icAmTE4WI @ 00:06:24]. Red sellers stay in follow-up for up to 2.5 years [Sumner Healey — R4icAmTE4WI @ 00:08:35], because someone who says no in April can turn around and sell in June.

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when every target county clears the 200-sale floor, the scrub removes flood, wetland, slope, and access problems, offers are hand-priced from comps and acreage bands, a merged proof has been checked, and six months of mailing runway sits in a dedicated account.

worksheets.title: Outbound Acquisition, Compliance, and List Building
worksheets.purpose: Choose and budget outbound channels, write compliant openers, scrub every list against registries and litigator files, and build stacked raw-land lists from public-record data verified at the Recorder before the first dial or text.
instructions: Fill in the channel and budget fields first, because channel math decides how many records you need to buy and which platform fits.
Write openers, scripts, and scrub schedules word for word so a partner or assistant can run them exactly without improvising.
Test every filter setting on a small pull before buying the full county export, and record any field that comes back empty or broken.
Log the scrub date for every list and every campaign so compliance can be proven later if a demand letter ever arrives.
Review your texts-per-contract and calls-per-lead numbers monthly and replace practitioner benchmarks with your own results once you have three months of data.

fields.name: channel_start_choice
fields.prompt: Pick the first outbound channel you will launch, whether texting, cold calling, or mail, and defend the choice using cost per contract, your skill level, and the sellers each channel reaches on the same county list.
fields.example: Launch with texting, because if I were to start over I'd start with texting first [Apke Brothers — Ls2lelB6ImM @ 00:16:11]. Budget assumes $1,300 to $1,500 per contract from A/B-tested openers and automated follow-ups [Dylan Applegate — Hyk7GilIJ8g @ 00:13:37]. Mail joins in month three, since calling, texting and mail reach different sellers on the same county list, as Michael Bull observes.

fields.name: texts_per_contract_benchmark
fields.prompt: Set your own texts-per-contract benchmark for a beginner and for a skilled texter. Multiply your planned monthly send volume by those ratios and write how many contracts per month that volume realistically produces at each skill level.
fields.example: Skilled benchmark is about 10,000 texts per contract; unskilled is 30,000 to 40,000 [Michael Bull — PMSn1EaZ42Y @ 00:06:01]. At 100,000 texts a month, that is only three contracts a month on the weaker ratio [Michael Bull — PMSn1EaZ42Y @ 00:06:15]. The Apke Brothers range of one per 5,000 skilled versus one per 20,000 beginner sets the stretch goal.

fields.name: text_opener_compliance
fields.prompt: Draft your first outbound text word for word. Confirm it states who you are, who you are contacting, and the marketing purpose, stays near 100 characters, and contains nothing casual or cryptic that could become screenshot evidence later.
fields.example: Opener: 'Hi, this is Dana with Ridge Land Co, reaching out to the owner of the parcel on County Road 12 about buying it.' It names the sender, the recipient, and the marketing purpose [REIPrintMail — L4oZCP8R6RQ @ 00:14:59]. From a TCPA perspective, calls and texts are the exact same thing, so the same rules apply [REIPrintMail — L4oZCP8R6RQ @ 00:13:11].

fields.name: dnc_litigator_scrub
fields.prompt: Document your compliance scrub schedule. List each registry and litigator database you will run before first contact, how often the scrub repeats, and the deadline your team follows for honoring removal requests once a seller asks to stop.
fields.example: Before first contact and every 30 days after, the list runs against the national and state DNC registries plus LexisNexis, Blacklist Alliance, and Contact Center Compliance litigator files, and removals are honored within 10 business days [REIPrintMail — L4oZCP8R6RQ @ 00:30:55]. The scrub date and file version are logged on every campaign sheet for audit.

fields.name: honey_pot_screen
fields.prompt: Write the warning signs that tell you a seller may be a honey pot setting up a TCPA demand letter. Describe exactly how you will respond when an overeager seller pushes for the purchase and sale agreement before any real negotiation.
fields.example: Red flags: feigned motivation, no questions about price, and repeated demands for paperwork, because what they're waiting for is for you to send them the purchase and sale agreement for their property [Ryan Dossey — hzDGK6PCjPg @ 00:02:41]. Response: pause, verify ownership and the contact record, and send nothing until the lead passes review.

fields.name: list_stacking
fields.prompt: Explain how you will stack lists before any outreach. Name the distress lists you will overlay, such as code violations, pre-foreclosure, or tax delinquency, and assign each stack tier its own treatment of hand-dials, texts, video, or power dialer.
fields.example: Tier 1 is code violations stacked with tax delinquency, which gets hand-dials, texts, and a 20-second video; single-list records get the power dialer and text blast [Maximilian Dier — xPy40xTlt64 @ 00:04:41]. Stacked government lists run about 1,000 records per deal versus 12,000 on regular data, roughly 10x better, so Tier 1 gets the best callers [Maximilian Dier — xPy40xTlt64 @ 00:22:01].

fields.name: raw_land_filter
fields.prompt: Write the exact filter settings you will use to isolate raw land on your data platform. Include improvement value, acreage range, land-use codes, and owner location, and note any field on that platform known to be poorly populated or broken.
fields.example: Improvement value set to 0 so only parcels with no improvements remain [Apke Brothers — tZnXE47jWp4 @ 00:02:39]. Acreage range 1 to 100.01, so the filter does not round to 99.99 and drop parcels [PRYCD — 7jGQIvwqBwc @ 00:07:50]. Owner mailing address must sit outside the county, and PropStream improvement-value fields get spot-checked before trusting the final pull.

fields.name: data_platform_cost
fields.prompt: Compare the per-record cost of the data platforms you are considering, such as DataTree, PropStream, PRYCD, or free county GIS. Estimate your total list cost after deduping owners, and note which platform also delivers offer pricing.
fields.example: DataTree exports run $0.10 per record with membership, and deduping owners lowers the charge, though the deduped count is not shown in advance [Apke Brothers — tZnXE47jWp4 @ 00:07:14]. PRYCD priced 300 records for $24, with the offer price included at a 25% default slider [PRYCD — 7jGQIvwqBwc @ 00:20:36]. Estimated list of 5,000 deduped records costs about $500.

fields.name: ownership_source_verification
fields.prompt: Describe how you will confirm current ownership before an offer goes out. Name the county office you treat as the source of truth, the layers you treat as secondary, and how you request bulk files when a clerk resists.
fields.example: Ownership comes from the Recorder, not the Assessor or GIS layer, which update later and can be stale [Country Land Sellers — 6qNh515jvww @ 00:04:53]. When a clerk resists, the request is framed as a private tax-paying citizen doing private independent research, with the file asked for in Excel [Zach Ginn — 3VKazhO11yk @ 00:04:24]. Mismatches get pulled from the campaign.

fields.name: budget_channel_math
fields.prompt: Run your monthly marketing budget against channel math before dialing. Using the calls-per-lead and leads-per-deal ratios, show how many records, dials, and weeks of work one deal requires, and state whether cold calling fits your budget.
fields.example: At 1,000 calls per lead and 30 leads per deal, one deal needs about 30,000 dials, so 10,000 records get called three times [Maximilian Dier — KmEcpx-t8YM @ 00:01:55]. With only $1,000 a month, cold calling is off the table, because a VA yields only one to two good leads a day [Maximilian Dier — uQ2jDRUrtoY @ 00:33:47]. Texting takes that budget instead.

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when the opening channel fits the monthly budget, every opener names sender, recipient, and purpose, registry and litigator scrubs are scheduled every 30 days, the honey-pot response is written, and raw-land filters are proven on a test pull.

worksheets.title: Comping, Pricing, and Due Diligence
worksheets.purpose: Value each parcel from sold land-only comps in a tight size band, adjust for wetlands, soils, and access, and run perc, septic, survey, and overlay checks inside the diligence window while walking away is still possible.
instructions: Complete one copy of this worksheet for every parcel under contract, and attach the exported comp list and overlay screenshots.
Start the comp search as narrow as possible on size, time, and distance, and widen only when too few sold comps remain.
Order soil, septic, and survey work the same day the contract is signed, because scheduling delays eat the diligence window.
Write the end buyer's exit next to every cost so septic, access, and survey findings are judged against what the buyer will actually build.
If any field reveals a deal killer, amend to extend closing before earnest money goes hard, or cancel inside the inspection period.

fields.name: comp_window_size_band
fields.prompt: Define your comp rules for one target parcel: the sold-only requirement, the acreage band around the subject, the lookback window in months, and the radius. Explain why larger tracts cannot be compared directly to a small lot.
fields.example: Subject is 8 acres, so comps stay between 5 and 10 acres sold in the last six to twelve months, because 36 and 50 acre sales cannot be compared with 8 as price per acre shrinks with size [Cool Wholesaling+ Land Deals-Real Estate Investing — 3x8J7AdyCEw @ 00:01:22]. Start as narrow as possible and only expand if needed.

fields.name: price_per_acre_calc
fields.prompt: Build the price-per-acre average for your subject parcel from an exported sold list. Record the source, the number of comps used, the average per-acre value, and the resulting retail estimate, then write your target and maximum buy prices.
fields.example: Zillow sold comps of 5 acres at $30,000 and 9 acres at $50,000 put Fairmont retail at $5,000 to $6,000 an acre, so 8 acres is about $40,000 retail, with a target buy of $30,000 and a $35,000 maximum [Cool Wholesaling+ Land Deals-Real Estate Investing — 3x8J7AdyCEw @ 00:03:12]. Brent Bowers aims under 50 cents on the dollar.

fields.name: outlier_removal
fields.prompt: List each comp you removed from the average and the reason. Flag sales that sit landlocked behind the main road, carry wetlands or poor soils, or simply do not line up with the rest of the sold list before averaging.
fields.example: Removed a $6,500 sale that looks landlocked behind the main road, so it is probably not a good comp [Cool Wholesaling+ Land Deals-Real Estate Investing — t8XDRE0ZjFc @ 00:02:04]. Removed one high sale that did not line up with the rest, since one odd sale throws everything else off [REtipster — rYCHQ59jzhY @ 00:06:17]. Eleven comps remain for the final per-acre average.

fields.name: non_disclosure_method
fields.prompt: If your county sits in a non-disclosure state, describe your workaround for missing sold prices. Show the days-on-market haircut you apply to last list prices, which listings you exclude, and which websites supply self-reported sold prices.
fields.example: Haircuts on last list price: 0-15% at 1-90 days, about 20-30% at 3-6 months, 35% and up to 50% at 6-12 months, with listings older than one year excluded [Sumner Advanced — 8pB5HoHJ4Bk @ 00:04:05]. Land.com sold listings supply self-reported prices, usually accurate, while LandFlip shows only actives [Sumner Advanced — 8pB5HoHJ4Bk @ 00:05:17]. A trusted realtor opinion backs thin markets.

fields.name: demand_signals
fields.prompt: Record the demand signals you read from active listing pages in your target area. Note typical days on market, view counts, saves, and how long comparable lots have sat, then state whether the market reads as healthy or dead.
fields.example: Most Cedar Springs lots sit under 100 days, and one lot pulled 498 views in 57 days, which signals decent land demand [REtipster — 9cX2NuhnYro @ 00:13:12]. A comparison county showed 10 to 20 views and no saves after months, which reads as a dead market, so it is dropped. Sold comps outrank actives when setting price.

fields.name: realtor_blowout_price
fields.prompt: Write the script you will use when calling a local land realtor for pricing. Ask for the fast-sale number rather than the hopeful one, record the answer and timeframe, and note whether the realtor might become a buyer or listing partner.
fields.example: Script: 'What is the 30-day blowout price? I want the get it done number, not the pie in the sky one year from now number' [Brent Bowers — JNufnuENoDM @ 00:09:15]. Brent Bowers heard about $10,000 within 45 days on a parcel held at $285, then took the realtor's own $5,000 offer and closed four days later [Brent Bowers — JNufnuENoDM @ 00:07:30].

fields.name: overlay_screen
fields.prompt: Describe the five-to-ten-minute overlay screen you run on every parcel before offering. List each layer checked, including slope, access, wetlands, flood zone, and soils, and the threshold on each layer that kills or reprices the deal.
fields.example: Wetlands, flood zone, and soil layers are pulled before any acreage comp is trusted, because a lot about 40 percent wet with very poorly drained Kinault peat sold at 20,000 after an 85,000 ask [Acrewell Land Company — TbH_4hSsYHU @ 00:06:46]. Any parcel over 25% wet gets repriced; any with no visible access path gets killed pending records.

fields.name: perc_septic_plan
fields.prompt: For any parcel without city sewer, write your soil and septic verification plan. State who orders the perc test or site evaluation, the expected cost, how long scheduling takes, and confirm it finishes inside the due diligence window.
fields.example: County health department perc runs $150 to $1,500 [REtipster — yp6qPMTkjgE @ 00:02:04]. The evaluation is booked the day the contract is signed, since evaluator scheduling can eat weeks, and closing waits until results are back [Florida Land Facts — zWTn3NY8wqc @ 00:02:14]. On resale, the buyer verifies inside the inspection period instead of paying about $600 per test.

fields.name: septic_cost_vs_exit
fields.prompt: Price the septic system the soil actually demands and compare it to the end buyer's total build budget. Note conventional, mound, treatment unit, or drip costs, and decide whether the system cost kills the intended exit for that lot.
fields.example: A $30,000 to $50,000 alternative system kills a $5,000 lot meant for a $30,000 mobile home [Jack Bosch — nVJMPjUWdZw @ 00:09:46]. Conventional Florida installs run $10,000 to $15,000, often more than an $8,000 lot [Florida Land Facts — zWTn3NY8wqc @ 00:02:34]. This parcel needs a mound, so the exit shifts to a buyer with a larger build budget and longer timeline.

fields.name: survey_and_diligence_window
fields.prompt: Set your diligence timeline and survey policy. State the maximum hours standard diligence may take, when you order a survey, how you handle a failed test hole on a large tract, and how you protect earnest money if the deal is unsold.
fields.example: Standard diligence is capped at 48 hours max [Apke Brothers — j3-xqUjgb7k @ 00:29:06]. A survey is ordered on every purchase, since boundaries differ from GIS 25 to 30% of the time [REtipster — w08yc3MEaGE @ 00:10:54]. One failed hole gets retested elsewhere, as a 12-acre tract passed in one corner. Unsold deals get a 30-to-45-day extension amendment.

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when the subject is priced from cleaned sold comps, outliers are removed, wetlands, flood, slope, and soils are screened, the perc or site evaluation is back, septic cost fits the exit, and a survey is ordered before closing.

worksheets.title: Access, Easements, Flood Zones, and Subdivide Yield
worksheets.purpose: Confirm that every parcel has recorded legal access and a known flood status before it is priced, then test whether a split can legally and profitably multiply its value. A parcel without access, or a split without frontage, is not a deal until the paperwork proves otherwise.
instructions: Pull county deed records, recorded easements, and the FEMA flood map for the parcel before entering any offer price on this worksheet.
Treat a parcel as truly landlocked only when it lacks both legal access and a long-used physical road, and cut its value before you calculate the offer.
Never count permissive access as legal access; convert any informal driveway or shared lane into written, recorded access before resale.
For any subdivide, divide total frontage by the county minimum lot width, round down, and confirm road access and public frontage for every proposed lot.
Complete every field with real numbers and named sources, and leave no field blank; an unknown access or flood answer means the deal is not ready to price.

fields.name: access_status_verification
fields.prompt: Record whether the parcel has legal access, physical access, both, or neither. List the county records you checked for a recorded easement and any long-used road, then state plainly whether the parcel qualifies as truly landlocked before pricing begins.
fields.example: Ten rural acres show no recorded easement in county deed records and no long-used physical road across the neighboring tract. Following the Bosch rule, only a parcel lacking both legal and actual road access counts as truly landlocked, so this one qualifies and gets repriced before any offer [Land Profit Generator with Jack & Michelle Bosch — tfERI-RnheU @ 00:01:59].

fields.name: landlocked_value_haircut
fields.prompt: Enter the accessible market value, the landlocked value after your haircut, and the resulting offer. Show the percentage cut you applied and explain why the reduction comes before the offer rather than being negotiated away after the seller says yes.
fields.example: Accessible value $40,000; landlocked value $15,000 to $20,000 after cutting at least half; offer near $4,000. Bosch states that the moment a property proves landlocked, the value goes down and therefore the offer goes down, so the haircut is applied first and the offer is built from that reduced number [Land Profit Generator with Jack & Michelle Bosch — tfERI-RnheU @ 00:05:31].

fields.name: neighbor_easement_negotiation
fields.prompt: Name each adjoining owner who could grant an access strip, the price you plan to offer, and your fallback if they refuse or overprice. Note the spread between landlocked and accessible value that the easement would unlock for the flip.
fields.example: Adjoining owner to the north controls the shortest route to the county road; planned offer is $500, the price Bosch says a reasonable neighbor might ask. That payment unlocks the spread between a $20,000 landlocked value and a $40,000 accessible value. Fallback: sell as-is to a cash buyer at $12,000 to $15,000 [Land Profit Generator with Jack & Michelle Bosch — tfERI-RnheU @ 00:09:36].

fields.name: easement_appraisal_leverage
fields.prompt: If a neighbor overprices the easement, describe how you will reframe the valuation and estimate what litigation would cost. Record whether the route is the only option and how that fact sets the ceiling on your negotiating room.
fields.example: The neighbor wants far more than the strip is worth. The appraiser values the neighbor's diminution in value rather than the lot's gain, and notes that roughly $20,000 in legal fees likely wins an easement-by-necessity suit when the route is the only option, so negotiating room tops out near that litigation cost [dhall3000 — GpQWztIpKSo @ 00:05:17].

fields.name: permissive_vs_legal_access
fields.prompt: List every driveway, two-track, or shared lane currently used to reach the parcel. For each, state whether it rests on a recorded easement or mere permission, and describe how you will convert informal use into written, recorded access.
fields.example: A gravel driveway has crossed the neighbor's land for years without paperwork, which is permissive use that can be terminated at any time [Law Case Summaries — wij1Dm2XEX8 @ 00:01:14]. That history is also leverage: the crossed owner is already used to the access, so getting it in writing is easier [David Miller — orMrWlpfWj4 @ 00:03:10].

fields.name: flood_zone_lookup
fields.prompt: Record the FEMA flood zone shown for the parcel, the share of the lot inside any special flood hazard area, and whether planned building or renovation could exceed the threshold that triggers costly elevation requirements for the end buyer.
fields.example: Address entered into the flood map search bar in the top left corner; a lot of blue appeared along the rear line, signaling nearby flood hazards [LAVERNE MCGEE TV — ptM7-3KSnO4 @ 00:00:57]. Any build or renovation exceeding 50% of pre-improvement market value can trigger $30,000 to $100,000 or more in elevation costs [PushLeads — fXtOfFlKqmc @ 00:04:24].

fields.name: loma_decision
fields.prompt: If a survey suggests the parcel sits above base flood elevation but was mapped into a high-risk zone, estimate the cost of a letter of map amendment, the yearly premium savings, and what the amendment will not change.
fields.example: Survey shows the pad above BFE despite a high-risk mapping. Budget $1,500 to $5,000 for engineering and survey; a successful LOMA can cut premiums by $1,000 or more per year [PushLeads — fXtOfFlKqmc @ 00:04:43]. Buyer disclosure note: a LOMA does not change flood risk, and the property may still flood even after removal [Compass Land USA — bPbMFP-bGyU @ 00:03:48].

fields.name: subdivide_lot_yield
fields.prompt: Calculate how many lots the parcel can legally yield. Enter total road frontage, the county minimum lot width, the minimum lot size, and the result rounded down, then confirm physical road access and public frontage for every proposed lot.
fields.example: Total frontage is 1,300 feet against a 350-foot county minimum width; 1,300 divided by 350 rounds down to three lots, not four [Dr. Dirt l Land Investor — 7wJsf4BbLHY @ 00:54:54]. Each of the three lots was checked for physical road access and public frontage, because skipping that check is the biggest subdivision mistake [Clay Hepler — o_c7zC-iYqE @ 00:03:26].

fields.name: split_profit_model
fields.prompt: Model the bulk purchase price against the combined resale value of the smaller lots. List acquisition cost, survey or perc testing, buy-side and sale-side closing costs, the projected total from all lots, net profit, and the expected timeline.
fields.example: Eighty Minnesota acres worth about $180,000 whole were split into four lots that sold for $369,000. Costs included $2,000 buy-side closing, $5,000 in perc testing, and roughly $22,000 or 6% sale-side closing, for $134,000 total cost and $235,000 net in under six months [Clay Hepler — o_c7zC-iYqE @ 00:01:35]. Twenty-five acres at $125,000 split five ways sells for $250,000 [Apke Brothers — 8LneZstpCGY @ 00:01:56].

fields.name: subdivide_approval_risk
fields.prompt: Describe the approval path for the split: paper split, exempt plat, minor or major subdivision. Note application fees, expected timeline, utility and sewer checks, and whether the contract carries a rezoning contingency or multiple exits if a hearing is required.
fields.example: Rural Arizona paper split: about $400 application fee, a few hundred dollars for new legal descriptions, roughly six weeks, each piece over one acre with road access [Jack Bosch — JXUkA5K7RSc @ 00:06:56]. On infill, sewer depth and power cost were verified because dewatering pushed a $3,500 connection to about $17,000 [Kent Cliffe — Ie0jq4Go9is @ 00:06:04].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not move to pricing or marketing until legal access is recorded or the landlocked haircut is applied, the flood zone is documented with any elevation exposure priced, and every proposed lot passes the frontage-divided-by-minimum-width test with confirmed road access.

worksheets.title: Approvals, Encumbrances, Offers, and Title
worksheets.purpose: Treat the recorded file and the county rulebook as the real product, then structure the offer and closing so the spread survives. Perc contingencies, frontage, restrictions, severed rights, exit choice, earnest money, and title coverage are each a place where a profitable contract quietly turns into a loss.
instructions: Write every offer contingent on a perc test by a licensed local tester and confirm recorded frontage on a county approved road before signing.
Run a title search and pull the county clerk's deed abstract, recorded covenants, and the mineral chain before the buyer plans any change of use.
Present two offers on every lead, a fast cash number and a higher longer-close number, and re-send them in writing every 30 days.
Do not double close under a $15,000 spread, and call title companies until one confirms in writing that it will close both sides.
Collect non-refundable buyer earnest money and decide owner's, lender's, or open title coverage before the closing date is set.

fields.name: perc_contingency
fields.prompt: Write the perc test contingency for this offer. Name the licensed local tester, the expected test cost, how long results stay valid, and the septic system cost range you would face if the soil demands an alternative system.
fields.example: Offer is contingent on a perc test by a licensed local tester, budgeted near the $1,300 average, with a typical range of $750 to $1,900. Results stay valid 2 to 5 years, and if the soil fails a conventional layout, a mound system could run $15,000 to $30,000 [Barndo And Tiny Homes Vision — VIdzLB23cAw @ 00:03:30].

fields.name: road_frontage_and_legal_access
fields.prompt: Identify the road each parcel or proposed lot fronts and whether it is a county approved road. Record the recorded easement or frontage document, and estimate upgrade costs if a private drive must be brought to county specifications.
fields.example: Seller says neighbors let everyone use the dirt drive, but physical access is not legal access, and verbal access means nothing to lenders and title companies [Barndo And Tiny Homes Vision — VIdzLB23cAw @ 00:04:05]. Upgrading the drive would require about 20 feet of surface, 6 to 8 inches of base rock, and 40 to 50 feet of right-of-way [Tim Howell — rtRAjfGZ_nY @ 00:01:20].

fields.name: deed_restriction_search
fields.prompt: List every deed restriction, covenant, or CC&R found in the title search and county clerk's deed abstract. For each, note what it prohibits, who can lift it, and whether actual neighborhood compliance suggests it is still enforced.
fields.example: Deed abstract pulled before the buyer plans changes [US Realty Training — B_XnC97BYF8 @ 00:03:38]. A recorded covenant bars livestock even with no HOA. Only the original grantor or heirs can lift it, and one holdout heir makes removal challenging if not impossible [The Real Estate Lawyer — gP3fDaUu5Iw @ 00:03:13]. A neighborhood drive shows no horses, so no horses planned.

fields.name: hoa_covenant_pull
fields.prompt: Find the governing HOA's exact legal name and pull the recorded covenants. Record the search tools used, the recording reference, and any covenant that would block the buyer's intended use, such as RVs, livestock, or detached garages.
fields.example: Ran the Secretary of State corporations search to confirm the HOA's exact name, then pulled the recorded covenants from the gsccca.org index using 'view image,' with the broker covering printing [Real Estate Made Crystal Clear — okIP6dYiTD4 @ 00:08:27]. Covenants restrict RV parking on lots, so the RV-owner buyer pool is struck from the marketing plan.

fields.name: mineral_and_surface_rights
fields.prompt: Trace the mineral, timber, and grazing rights through the deed chain. Record any reservations, assignments, or releases, plus any conservation easement terms, and explain how each severed right changes what the end buyer actually receives at closing.
fields.example: Mineral chain followed through deeds, reservations, assignments, and releases; HOA ownership of common property does not automatically mean ownership of minerals under lots [HOA LAND WARS — CnlqGcAGqOo @ 00:05:01]. A wetland reserve easement covers the back forty: crops cannot be pulled off it, and hunting leases are the number one income generator on such land [MissStateExtension — UkiDG5GpG_Y @ 00:02:46].

fields.name: two_offer_structure
fields.prompt: Draft the two offers you will present on this lead: a fast cash number and a higher number closing in 90 to 120 days. Record each price, its percentage of market value, and the follow-up date for re-sending in writing.
fields.example: Cash offer at $85,000 now; longer-close offer at $117,000 in 90 days, mirroring the Apke example in which about 50% of the hosts' deals were not the highest offer [Apke Brothers — lWYFLEd7PA0 @ 00:19:10]. Both offers are mailed in writing and re-sent every 30 days within a five sellers a day conversation routine [Flipping Mastery TV — YPqUHvSAZrU @ 00:02:26].

fields.name: exit_structure_choice
fields.prompt: Choose between cash close, assignment, and double close for this deal. Record the purchase price as a percentage of market value, the projected spread, doubled closing costs, and the specific question mark on the deal or market justifying a double close.
fields.example: Contract sits at 48% of market value, under Michael Bull's 50% cash-close threshold, so the plan is to buy outright [Michael Bull — V4qnHYV6EVo @ 00:11:38]. A second lead with a $10,000 spread would net about $4,000 after $5,000 to $6,000 in doubled closing costs, so it gets assigned instead of double closed [Flip With Rick — 4Ueirfxr5Ww @ 00:05:40].

fields.name: title_company_confirmation
fields.prompt: Before signing the purchase contract, list the title companies you called, which ones confirmed they will close both sides, any state cooling-off rule involved, and whether blind or split settlement statements are available and at what added fee.
fields.example: Following Hepler's approach on a Georgia deal, where the seven-day cooling-off period blocked the back close, kept dialing until the ninth of eleven title companies agreed to close both sides, saving a $28,000 spread on 38 acres [Clay Hepler — IRJeZQijnxU @ 00:08:08]. Also asked which offices provide blind or split HUDs, sometimes for an added fee [Flip With Rick — 4Ueirfxr5Ww @ 00:13:39].

fields.name: buyer_earnest_money
fields.prompt: Record the end buyer's name, the non-refundable earnest money amount collected, the date it was received, and the spread on the deal. Explain how you will respond if the buyer resists the deposit or demands a different closing structure.
fields.example: Buyer deposit set at $1,000 non-refundable, above the $500 floor, because legitimate buyers will pay it [Sumner Advanced — zyoO3FxrTDQ @ 00:02:25]. Spread is $22,000, clearing the $15,000 double-close minimum. If the buyer pushes to restructure the closing, the deal is not switched to satisfy a difficult buyer; the buyer is replaced instead [Flip With Rick — 4Ueirfxr5Ww @ 00:13:39].

fields.name: title_insurance_plan
fields.prompt: Specify the title insurance coverage for both your purchase and the resale. Note whether an owner's policy is being purchased on a cash or vacant land buy, and whether an open policy can avoid paying for two new policies.
fields.example: Cash purchase, so there is no lender's policy at all [House Cashers LLC — Up2OF5KmfcU @ 00:00:31]; an owner's policy is ordered because a lender policy gives the buyer zero direct legal protection. Resale expected within about a year, so an open title insurance policy is purchased to avoid paying for two new policies [Sumner Advanced — zyoO3FxrTDQ @ 00:01:06].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not sign or assign until the perc contingency is written, county approved frontage or a recorded easement is confirmed, every restriction and severed right is listed, the exit clears its spread floor, a title company has confirmed both sides, and buyer earnest money is in hand.

worksheets.title: Selling on Terms, Buyer Assets, Drone Media, and Alternative Land Uses
worksheets.purpose: Turn the inventory into cash flow by pricing on terms, staying inside the vacant land exemptions and originator thresholds, treating buyers as the real asset, and shooting media that sells acreage. Then test whether repositioning the land into RV, solar, or battery storage use earns more than a straight resale.
instructions: Set a cash price and a terms price for every parcel, multiply the terms price out, and compare both against acquisition cost.
Keep each seller-financed sale vacant with a no-build-before-payoff clause and count owner-occupant deals per person, not per LLC, against state thresholds.
Run the high-cost test on APR rather than the note rate, and schedule early-payoff reminders before each cashback window closes.
Research parcel lines, FAA restrictions, and the survey before any drone flight, and qualify every buyer by zip code, county, and subdivision.
Before pursuing RV, solar, or battery storage use, model site conversion, underwrite only contracted payments, and clear zoning and permitting first.

fields.name: terms_vs_cash_pricing
fields.prompt: Set both a cash price and a seller-financed terms price for the parcel. Record the down payment, monthly payment, term length, and total terms price multiplied out, and compare the result against your acquisition cost and target sales mix.
fields.example: Bought near $10,000, priced to sell near $20,000 on terms with 10% down and about $500 a month, following Abhi's model of roughly 80% terms and 20% cash [REtipster — HpkNhY7WclQ @ 00:09:39]. Terms price multiplied out the way Jeff does it: 297 down plus 97 a month for 48 months totals 4,953 [Jeff — mM0tCRujCDM @ 00:01:52].

fields.name: dodd_frank_vacant_check
fields.prompt: Confirm the sale qualifies as vacant land sold to a non-occupant. Record the no-build-before-payoff clause wording, whether any structure or manufactured home could go on within two years, and how you protect the land exemption for this note.
fields.example: Buyer plans recreational use only. A no-build-before-payoff clause is added because RESPA's land exemption fails if a structure or manufactured home goes on within 2 years using loan proceeds [REtipster — m1GoTr9J5TM @ 00:17:36]. Vacant land seems excluded from the special rules in subpart E [REtipster — m1GoTr9J5TM @ 00:09:01], so the clause keeps the note inside that exclusion.

fields.name: rmlo_threshold_tracker
fields.prompt: Count owner-occupant seller-financed deals you have personally written this year against your state's residential mortgage loan originator threshold. Record the threshold, deals already closed, whether entity stacking is relied upon, and when a licensed originator must be brought in.
fields.example: Texas operator holding four owner-occupant notes this year, counted per person rather than per LLC, against thresholds of Texas 5, Colorado 3, and California 0 [William Bronchick — ZGvGq-_10yA @ 00:08:25]. One more owner-occupant note fits before a licensed originator is needed. Entity stacking is skipped, since critics call it a blatant attempt to evade [Seller Finance Consultants, Inc. — SB_vfxPYuF8 @ 00:00:43].

fields.name: high_cost_and_rate_structure
fields.prompt: Record the note rate, the calculated APR including fees, and the high-cost threshold you are testing against. If balloons are barred, describe any escalating-rate structure you plan to use to encourage the buyer to refinance early.
fields.example: High-cost test run on APR, not the note rate, and the note stays under it, following Bronchick's rule: just don't have a high-cost mortgage [William Bronchick — MNznbFmtOwI @ 00:28:44]. Because balloons are barred, rates escalate from 6 to 8 to 10 to 12%, making buyers cry uncle and refinance, which mimics a balloon [William Bronchick — ZGvGq-_10yA @ 00:23:53].

fields.name: early_payoff_cashback
fields.prompt: Design the early-payoff incentive for this note. Record the cashback percentage for each payoff window, the months when reminders go out, and the expected share of borrowers who accept, compared with selling the note outright to an investor.
fields.example: Four-year land note offers 5% back on payoff within 6 months and 2.5% within 12 months; about 10% of borrowers take it [REtipster — HpkNhY7WclQ @ 00:11:17]. Reminders are scheduled in months 4 to 5 and 9 to 11 so buyers act before each window closes [REtipster — HpkNhY7WclQ @ 00:20:04]. The cash pulled forward replaces selling notes or borrowing from funders.

fields.name: buyer_list_asset
fields.prompt: Describe how you will build and qualify your buyer list for this parcel. Record your current cost per buyer lead, the channels used, and the zip codes, counties, and subdivisions each buyer has confirmed interest in.
fields.example: Buyers are treated as the real asset because acquisition cost climbed from about $5 per Facebook lead to $800 to $1,200 per lead [REtipster — HpkNhY7WclQ @ 00:42:14]. Sellers get texts, but every buyer gets a call and is qualified by zip code, city, county, and subdivision in the Flip Force CRM [DGB Media — 4KWC7a6vLcY @ 00:39:07].

fields.name: drone_shot_plan
fields.prompt: Plan the aerial media for this listing. Record the pilot's certification, the FAA airspace check, how the survey lines will be shown, the lens and distance used to avoid neighbors, and the shots that sell acreage and surroundings.
fields.example: Before flight, the parcel is researched with Google Earth, FAA restrictions, and the survey so the lot lines and airspace are known [Matt Wood — ZU1aoe6pwQI @ 00:02:26]. The pilot holds Part 107 certification and delivers an add-on package at $125 for five photos or $225 for ten, about five minutes of shooting time [Wyman Gentry — ItWPpkhNHto @ 00:03:51].

fields.name: rv_use_underwriting
fields.prompt: If the parcel could become an RV park or RV storage lot, record the usable site conversion percentage, number of spaces, entry cap rate, projected NOI, and the zoning and permitting status required before any units are built.
fields.example: Five-acre, $2M RV storage build modeled two ways: 240 spaces returns about 12% cash-on-cash, while 160 spaces returns roughly 1%, because poor layout drops conversion to 40% and NOI from about $190k to $115k [The Owner's Math — xjNh4eemKCs @ 00:18:13]. Zoning cleared first, since one glamping student was shut down for 6-plus months [Heather Blankenship — FY9TF9ZkLwk @ 00:32:00].

fields.name: solar_lease_terms
fields.prompt: If a solar developer approaches the landowner, record the option period length, annual rent per acre, escalator, lease term, and whether leased acreage matches optioned acreage. Note your plan for selling the lease stream once construction starts.
fields.example: Offer reviewed: 4-5 year option, then a 30-year lease at $300 to $2,000 per acre per year with a 2% escalator [LandApp by LandGate — Uaymin1wo40 @ 00:03:33]. Underwrite only lease payments and match lease acreage to optioned acreage, since the developer can terminate during the option. Once construction starts, investors pay huge premiums for the stream [LandApp by LandGate — Uaymin1wo40 @ 00:05:18].

fields.name: battery_storage_site
fields.prompt: For a battery storage inquiry, record parcel acreage, distance to the substation, the offered purchase price per acre, and the zoning or planning approvals needed. Explain why this use is typically sold rather than leased by the landowner.
fields.example: Fifteen-acre parcel near a substation drew an offer at $30,000 per acre, or $450,000 total. Storage sites of 5 to 15 acres are bought outright rather than leased because the substation is deeded to the utility [LandApp by LandGate — Uaymin1wo40 @ 00:09:18]. Counterpoint noted for the file: Texas batteries reportedly eat their own lunch.

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not list or close a terms sale until the terms price is multiplied out, the no-build clause is in the note, owner-occupant deals are counted per person against the state threshold, APR clears the high-cost test, and any alternative use has zoning cleared and only contracted payments underwritten.
